newsitem.title: QATAR: Gulf alliance yet to realise integration dream.
newsitem.headline: Gulf alliance yet to realise integration dream.

text.p: Following are issues likely to surface at the annual summit on Saturday of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) which comprises Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Oman.

BORDER DISPUTES: The most sensitive issue, described by some GCC states as "time bombs". Bahrain says it will not attend the summit because of its dispute with host Qatar over a cluster of islands and reefs. The GCC had set a target to settle border disputes by the time of the previous summit a year ago.

"TERRORISM" AND SECURITY: All six states, realising Islamic fundamentalism could grow and find fertile ground in their conservative oil-rich states, have pledged to fight "extremism" and "terrorism". But a joint security pact still faces difficulties despite years of discussions, with some concerned over the extradition of citizens wanted in other GCC states and cross-border hot pursuit of suspects.

ECONOMIC INTEGRATION: A Gulf common market has long eluded the GCC which needs unified customs tariffs to facilitate a free trade accord with major blocks like the European Union and open markets for cheap Gulf petrochemicals. Although some obstacles had been removed in recent years, those meeting in Doha will face the same problems that have always blocked a common market.
